results.corrected_title: Chip stocks fall eight days in a row, longest losing streak since 2008
results.corrected_summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 3.8% on Friday 16 October 2026. It was the index's eighth straight losing session and its longest losing run since 2008. The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.5% on the day and posted its worst week in about 18 months, and AMD dropped 5.95%. Reports blamed doubts about AI spending, a 10-year Treasury yield of 5.10%, oil above $100 and fears of another Fed rate hike. Bank of America's Sebastian Raedler noted that consensus forecasts for hyperscaler capex have tripled from $330bn in early 2025 to $1tn.
key_facts: SOX -3.8% on 16 Oct 2026, eighth straight decline, longest streak since 2008
Reuters: the SOX lost over $1.6tn in market value (an 11.6% slide) over six sessions to mid-October
Nasdaq 100 -2.5% on 16 Oct and its worst week in about 18 months; AMD -5.95%, Intel -5.79%, Micron -5.63%
10-year Treasury yield at 5.10% (15 Oct); WTI crude at $101.91 (14 Oct)
BofA: consensus hyperscaler capex forecasts tripled from $330bn to $1tn
results.issues: The close of 11,137 was not confirmed in any source, though it matches Reuters' Thursday close of 11,581 minus 3.8%. The '>11% on the week' figure was not confirmed. The '$1.6T in six days' figure comes from Reuters (11.6% over six sessions), not from the Bloomberg URL, which I did not open; the Bloomberg headline mentions $1tn. Some mid-session reports said the streak was the longest since 2006, but closing coverage says 2008. The '$1tn+ lost by tech stocks' figure in 24/7 Wall St. has no source given.

results.corrected_title: CoreWeave debt fears hit Oracle and neocloud stocks
results.corrected_summary: CoreWeave, which has about $50bn in debt, fell more than 15.5% on 14 October 2026 after a viral chart showed one of its bonds yielding above 15%. Oracle fell 8.8% the same day, and other neoclouds also fell. Reuters reported that CoreWeave's credit default swaps rose to about 1,000bp, implying a roughly 63% chance of default within five years, and that its April-issued bonds traded near 79 cents on the dollar. The stock was heading for a weekly loss of nearly 25% by Friday 16 October. Nvidia owns about 10% of CoreWeave and has committed to buy unsold capacity through April 2032. Jensen Huang said Nvidia sees no need to backstop the company.
key_facts: CoreWeave -15.5%+ on 14 Oct; weekly loss nearing 25% on 16 Oct (Reuters)
About $50bn in debt; CDS about 1,000bp, implying roughly 63% five-year default probability; April bonds near 79 cents
Oracle -8.8% on 14 Oct; Nebius -10%, Applied Digital and IREN -9% each on 16 Oct
Nvidia holds about 10% and will buy unsold capacity through 13 April 2032; Huang said no backstop is needed
Gartner (15 Oct): about 80% of neoclouds could shut down by 2030
results.issues: The US News URL timed out; the same Reuters weekly story was confirmed through search results. The peer declines happened on different days: Oracle on 14 Oct, and Nebius, Applied Digital and IREN on 16 Oct per Reuters. One outlet put the weekly drop at about 22% depending on timing. The Gartner forecast is a projection, not a fact.

results.corrected_title: Anthropic reports $16.8bn Q3 revenue and adjusted profit at pre-IPO investor day; some investors discuss ~$1.5T valuation
results.corrected_summary: Unnamed attendees told Reuters that Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of $16.8bn at an investor day at its San Francisco headquarters on 14 October 2026. That is up 45% from $11.6bn in Q2, and the company said it was profitable on an adjusted basis. Reuters reported on 15 October that some investors, disappointed by the slower quarter-on-quarter growth, discussed a valuation of about $1.5tn instead of the roughly $2tn previously floated for the proposed November share sale. Reuters has also reported that the listing could slip until after the US midterm elections.
key_facts: Investor day on 14 Oct 2026 at Anthropic HQ in San Francisco, with CEO Dario Amodei and CFO Krishna Rao
Profitable on an adjusted basis in Q3 (per attendees)
Some investors discussed about $1.5tn versus the roughly $2tn target
Commitment of at least $518bn over a decade on cloud and compute
results.issues: The figures come from unnamed attendees and Anthropic did not comment, so confidence is medium. The RTÉ URL was not opened. IPO timing is uncertain: November was proposed, but Reuters also reported it could come after the midterms.
